section_summary.extract_value: This section discusses a single, unnamed study (Study X) that evaluated the Polish translation of the BAS-2, reporting a one-factor structure, full scalar invariance across sex, adequate internal consistency, and convergent validity. The authors report no significant sex differences in total BAS-2 scores and note a negative correlation between body appreciation and BMI; they also indicate BMI was based on self-reported height and weight and that sampling was accidental. Limitations highlighted include non-random (accidental) sampling, potential bias from self-reported BMI, and the absence of test-retest reliability and some validity assessments.
section_summary.evidence_source: EFA and CFA supported a one-dimensional factor structure of the BAS-2, which is in line with the original, English version of the scale (Tylka & Wood-Barcalow, 2015). Men and women did not differ significantly in total scores. The present study, similarly to other reports (Avalos et al., 2005; Swami et al., 2011), also found negative correlations between body appreciation and BMI. Second, BMI might have been biased by inaccuracies in self-reported weight and height. First, accidental but not random sampling was used, which may have led to an under/overrepresentation of certain groups within participants.
